FAs of children with CM in Malawi have demonstrated scattered areas of capillary non-perfusion which equate to the clinical finding of retinal whitening (Fig. 2) [14, 17]. Sequestration of pRBCs occurs initially in capillaries and post-capillary venules, so it is logical that the ischaemia is in multiple small zones rather than large blocks of tissue as supplied by arterioles. It is likely that the pattern of ischaemia in the retina is mirrored in the brain. Follow up of patients with hyper-reflectivity on OCT scans due to ischaemia shows retinal thinning and atrophy at one year (Fig. 3) [22].
